label: Test which giver acts through a secondary esse cause
summary: See docs/notes/q44-inferential-dependency.md, When does the giver act through the agent? Binary per se composition plus the caused-cause bridge and excluded middle yield the original composition premise. The equal-giver case uses the existing last edge. In the distinct case the named giver witnesses the upstream actual cause needed by the bridge. The binary marker still has no giver index. Application-indexed causal credit and alignment of every preceding giver with the applier imply the binary law. The four-role control preserves positive indexed credit and existential application while separating the two-giver assignment from universal binary composition. Actual transmission through the operating secondary agent provides positive, defeasible evidence in the ordinary cases. Source withdrawal alone is neither a named contribution nor a test of which causal role is exercised.
blocker: No independent universal warrant that each actual esse giver of the intermediary applies it in every per se exercise. Identity of a patient’s change with an agent’s action cannot identify that giver. For universal transfer to a further respect the effect-level alignment still needs warrant on the same source, bearer and actuality.
